messages.content: i cooked for my sister today. it was only a simple meal, but i was happy when she asked for more.
that sounds like a part of the day you enjoyed. what did you make?
rice and vegetables. i usually cook for myself, so having someone else there felt different.
you had someone to share the table with and someone who could tell you what they liked. was that the part you enjoyed most, or was it making the meal for her?
i think i liked seeing her sit down after work and rest for a while.
then the food was one way to give her a little time without work. a simple meal can still give someone a good break. you liked having time with her after work.
say that simply.
the meal gave you time together while she could rest after work.
help me write a short message saying she can come again if she wants.
i enjoyed cooking for you today. you are welcome to come for another meal when you have time.
should i say i know she enjoyed it very much?
only if she told you that. you can say she asked for more, but her feeling is still hers to give.
answer simply.
you can say she asked for more. ask how she felt rather than choosing her answer.
can we talk about music? ask me one question at a time, please.
what kind of music do you enjoy?
i like quiet music when i draw.
what do you like about having music while you draw?
it makes the room feel less empty. i do not want teaching about music, just a conversation.
then we can keep talking about your own time with it. do you usually choose a song you know or something new?
i choose music i know.
what is one thing you like about knowing the song already?
i can listen without thinking hard about every word.
the music gives you sound in the room while you think about the picture. it does not need to become another task.
use sound in the room.
the music gives you sound in the room while you think about the picture. it does not need to become another task.
now stop asking and tell me what you understood from my answers.
you like quiet music you already know while drawing. it makes the room feel less empty, and you can listen without thinking hard about every word.
i want a message asking a group to read a plan today but saying they can answer tomorrow. make the order clear.
please read the plan today. you can give your answer tomorrow.
say my request simply.
ask the group to read today and answer tomorrow, with the difference clear.
why not say please finish it today?
finish it could sound like both reading and answering must be done today. read the plan today gives the part you really need today.
explain simply.
finish it could sound like both reading and answering must be done today. your message only asks for reading today.
now one person asks if they must give an answer before lunch tomorrow. i do not have a specific hour in mind.
you could say: any time tomorrow is fine. there is no need to answer before lunch.
if i need it before dinner instead, should you add that without me saying it?
no. before dinner is a new detail you have not given. i should ask or keep tomorrow general as you said.
answer simply.
no. before dinner is a new detail you have not given. i should keep tomorrow general unless you choose an hour.
i saw a film about two friends who go to a village, but i do not know how to tell someone about it in simple words.
you can begin with who it is about and what they do: it is about two friends going to a village. what is one thing that happens there?
use go and write the first part simply.
then you could say: two friends go to a village and find an old house. they try to learn who lived there.
one thinks it was a teacher, but the other thinks it was a doctor. do not choose who is right.
two friends go to a village and try to learn who lived in an old house. they have different ideas about who it was.
can you ask me what happens next instead of making it up?
what do they do to find out more about the house?
they ask a woman in the garden next to it. stop the short story there.
two friends go to a village and find an old house. they have different ideas about who lived there, so they ask a woman in the garden next to it.
what did i want you not to do?
you wanted me to stop before giving the answer about who lived there. that fact has not been given yet.
i was making a picture with my cousin. i wanted blue, and she wanted green. we used both.
which part did you make with blue, and what did she make with green?
i used blue for water, and she used green for plants.
then both choices had a place in the picture. did you choose that together from the start, or work it out after talking?
we talked first. at the start we each wanted the whole thing in one color.
you changed from choosing one color for everything to finding a part for each idea. that can make a picture feel like something both people helped shape.
shape is in the list. can you write a short story from just those facts?
i wanted blue, and my cousin wanted green. we talked, then used blue for water and green for plants. both ideas were in the picture.
make it simple.
we talked and chose blue for water and green for plants. both ideas had a place in the picture.
does that mean nobody gives up an idea when making something together?
no. it is one example of finding room for both ideas. another task could need a different choice.
answer simply.
no. this picture had room for both ideas, but every task can be different.
my father kept an old picture i drew. i think my new pictures are better, so i do not know why he still likes that one.
he may like the memory of when you made it, or a part that is important to him. you can ask what he likes rather than choose his answer yourself.
give a simple question.
what do you like about this picture?
he says he can remember me drawing it at the kitchen table while he cooked.
then the picture brings back time together for him. it can be important even if your drawing has changed after that day.
say it simply.
he can remember time with you when he sees it. your new drawing can be better while the old one still has that memory.
write a short note i can keep with the picture.
my father kept this picture from a day when i drew at the kitchen table while he cooked.
can i add that he thinks it is the best picture in the world?
only if he said that. he can like the memory without saying it is the best picture of all.
answer simply.
he can like the memory without saying it is the best picture of all.
i have many things to do this morning and keep thinking about every task at once. help me choose one place to start, but ask what needs to be ready first.
what needs to be ready first this morning?
my school letter needs to be ready before lunch. cleaning my room can wait.
then begin with the letter. you can leave the room task for later because it does not need to be ready first.
i do not know the first sentence yet.
start with the thing you most need the teacher to know. write the important idea first in simple words. then you can change the sentence if you want it better.
say it simply.
write the idea first. you can work on the words after that.
the idea is that i need another day to return a book.
you could start: could i return the book tomorrow instead of today?
does that ask the teacher for a different time or say i have chosen already?
it asks whether the change is okay. it does not say the teacher has already said yes.
what should i do next before cleaning the room?
finish the message you need before lunch. then choose what to do with the room after that task is ready.
my teacher asked me to explain one sentence in my story. i thought that made the whole story wrong.
a question about one sentence does not tell you that. the teacher may want more detail or may want to understand what you had in mind.
say my first message simply.
my teacher asked about one sentence, and i thought the whole story was wrong.
what can i ask to understand what help is needed?
you could say: which part of this sentence is not clear, and what would help make the idea clear?
what if the teacher says the sentence is clear but they want to know why i chose it?
then it is a question about your choice, rather than a request to fix a wrong sentence. you can tell them the idea you wanted the sentence to give.
write a reply if i wanted it to make the person seem lonely.
i chose that sentence because i wanted the person to seem lonely in that part of the story.
does asking why always mean do not use it?
no. why can ask for a reason without asking you to change anything. the words and context help show which kind of question it is.
can you end by asking me what sentence they asked about?
what was the sentence your teacher wanted you to explain?
a game rule says choose a blue object. i choose a blue cup. does that mean every blue object has to be a cup?
no. the cup is one possible blue object. the rule asks for color, rather than a specific kind of object.
answer simply.
no. a blue cup can follow the rule, and another blue object can too.
use can follow in a short answer.
a blue cup can follow the rule. another blue object can too.
now the rule says choose a blue cup only. can i choose a blue book?
no. the new rule asks for a cup as well as blue. the book has the color but not the kind of object needed.
write a question asking whether the kind of object is important.
does it have to be a cup, or can it be any blue object?
say my last request simply.
ask whether the rule needs a cup or only a blue object.
can one new word make an old answer wrong for a new question?
yes. adding cup made the new rule more specific. an answer that worked for blue object may not work for blue cup.
is i walk before work the same as i walk for work?
not always. before work is about time. for work can be about the reason you walk or a task you do as part of working. those are different ideas.
write a short example for before work.
i take a quiet walk in the morning before going to the office. the walk is my own time, and the work starts later.
use office in a simple example.
i take a quiet walk in the morning before going to the office. the walk is my own time, and the work starts later.
now give an example with a worker bringing a letter to a house.
a worker walks to a house to bring a letter. the walking is part of that work, rather than only time before work.
use a letter to one house.
a worker walks to a house to bring a letter. the walking is part of that work.
does seeing someone walk tell me which reason is true?
no. you need more context about what they are doing and why. two people can both walk and have different reasons.
answer simply.
no. two people can both walk and have different reasons.
five people worked on a garden, but the photo only has three of them. can i say only those three helped?
not from the photo alone. a picture can leave people out. you already said five worked, so the photo should not make you forget the other two.
write a note for the photo that keeps both facts.
three of the five people who worked on the garden are in this photo.
what if i do not know who the other two people are?
you can know five helped without knowing who every person was. knowing the number and knowing each person are different things.
answer simply.
you can know five helped without knowing who every person was. do not change five to three just because only three are in the picture.
can i write thanks to everyone who helped?
yes. it can thank all five people, even when the photo has only three.
answer simply.
yes. you can thank everyone who helped, even if they are not in the photo.
write a short message for the group.
thank you to everyone who helped with the garden. i was happy to be part of the work.
picoboi, i want a short message about tomorrow. do not ask ten questions at once.
what do you want to say about tomorrow?
that i cannot come, but i want another day.
you could write: i cannot come tomorrow. could we choose another day?
can you make it for my aunt without adding a reason?
i cannot come tomorrow, but i would like to visit another day. would that work for you?
why did you not say i have school or work?
you asked for no reason, and you did not give one. a useful message can say the change and ask about another day without adding why.
answer simply.
you did not give a reason, so i kept it out. the message still says what changes and what you would like next.
what if i later say it is because i have work?
then i can add that: i cannot come tomorrow because i have work. could we choose another day for a visit?
does adding that reason mean i am never free?
no. it is a reason for tomorrow. it does not give your time for every other day.
